newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia corn stable, players await harvest.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia corn stable, players await harvest.

text.p: Indonesian corn prices remained weak on Tuesday amid ample stock levels at feedmills as players waited for the harvest before deciding on imports, traders said.
They said corn was quoted at 380-385 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from last week. Soymeal was holding at 850-860 rupiah/kg, unchanged from a week ago.
"Players are watching closely the harvest in East Java, which is expected next month," one trader said. "The next batch of imports will depend on the volume of the harvest."
The trader said he expected feedmills and traders to import between 400,000 and 500,000 tonnes of corn in the second half of this year, subject to the volume of the East Java harvest.
Another trader said stock levels of traders were running low, with some holding back sales due to weak prices.
"Many traders' stocks are quite low at the moment and they feel current prices are too low," he said. "Feedmills, however, have ample stocks and imports are continuing to arrive."
Traders also said they were relieved that the government had deferred a decision on imposing an import duty on corn.
Agriculture Minister Syarifuddin Baharsyah said last week the government was still studying whether to impose an import duty on corn or find other ways of boosting domestic prices.
"It looks like the duty might not be imposed because it runs against a move by Southeast Asian countries to lower import duties in the region," one trader said.
